references.text: Jesus warns the disciples that 'brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child,' and that they will be hated by all for his name's sake. This is a direct parallel to Luke 21:16, where family members hand over their own ([ref:Matt 10:21-22|Matthew 10:21-22]).

In Jesus' eschatological discourse in Matthew, he says that believers will be handed over to tribulation and killed, and that many will fall away and betray one another—the same theme of persecution and betrayal found in Luke 21:16 ([ref:Matt 24:9-10|Matthew 24:9-10]).

Mark's parallel to Luke 21:16: 'Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against parents and cause their death.' The same prophecy about family members betraying one another ([ref:Mark 13:12|Mark 13:12]).

The prophet Micah speaks of how a man's enemies are those of his own household: the son dishonors the father, the daughter rises against her mother. This Old Testament motif of family division underlies Jesus' prophecy in Luke 21:16 ([ref:Mi 7:6|Micah 7:6]).

Stephen's martyrdom is a fulfillment of Jesus' words that some of the disciples would be killed. He was handed over and stoned to death—a concrete illustration of 'they will kill some of you' ([ref:Apg 7:59-60|Acts 7:59-60]).
James, John's brother, was executed by the sword by King Herod—a direct fulfillment of Jesus' prophecy that some of the disciples would be killed ([ref:Apg 12:2|Acts 12:2]).

Jesus says that a time will come when those who kill the disciples will think they are doing God a service. This expands on the prophecy in Luke 21:16 that some of them will be put to death ([ref:Joh 16:2|John 16:2]).

Jesus quotes Micah 7:6 and says he has come to set a man against his father, a daughter against her mother—family division as the background for why family members will hand over believers, as described in Luke 21:16 ([ref:Matt 10:35-36|Matthew 10:35-36]).
